statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-48937 is a flaw in the Node.js HTTP/2 server: when the bundled nghttp2 library ended a session on its own because of a protocol error from the peer, it queued a GOAWAY frame without notifying Node.js, so the server kept the session open and kept accepting data after sending GOAWAY. Node.js fixed it for 22.x in 22.23.0, released 2026-06-18: the June 2026 security release, https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/june-2026-security-releases, lists Node.js 22 among the two affected release lines, and the 22.23.0 release notes, https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v22.23.0, list this CVE. The fix is commit https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/a1a5bb968303229d4a3a7c9e389dc3ece6237b4c ('deps: fix integration issues with the latest nghttp2'), which carries CVE-ID: CVE-2026-48937 and is in the v22.23.0 tag and not in v22.22.3; outside tests it changes src/node_http2.cc and src/node_http2.h, so that a GOAWAY frame sent by nghttp2 that Node.js did not initiate is detected when the frame is sent and the session is then failed with a protocol error and torn down. The CVE record, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-48937, lists Node.js 22 releases up to 22.22.3 as affected. The DHI nodejs-22 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from the upstream Node.js release tarball for their version. Each published nodejs-22 package holds one file, /usr/bin/node, a dynamically linked musl program that carries the Node.js JavaScript library and the C++ runtime where this code lives; the nodejs-22-dev subpackages hold C and C++ header files and two .gypi build configuration files under /usr/include/node, and the nodejs-22-doc subpackages hold the node man page and two debugger helper files, gdbinit and lldb_commands.py, with no ELF, PE or Mach-O file in either. The node binary links no system nghttp2 library (its only ELF NEEDED entries are libstdc++.so.6, libgcc_s.so.1 and the musl C library), so the HTTP/2 code is the copy compiled into it. We checked /usr/bin/node in every nodejs-22 package for Alpine 3.23 published by 2026-11-28, on x86_64 and aarch64 (checksums verified against the package index): 22.23.0-r0, 22.23.1-r0, 22.23.2-r0, 22.23.3-r0, 22.23.4-r0, 22.23.4-r1, 22.23.4-r2 and 22.23.5-r0 report v22.23.0 through v22.23.5 and carry the fix, while the earlier builds 22.22.0-r0, 22.22.1-r0, 22.22.2-r0, 22.22.2-r1 and 22.22.3-r0 report v22.22.0 through v22.22.3 and are affected. As a check, the debug message the fix adds to src/node_http2.cc, 'nghttp2 session terminated internally', is in the node binary of 22.23.0-r0 and every later build on both architectures and in none of the earlier builds, while a message from the same file that predates the fix, 'terminating session with code %d', is in every build. 22.23.0-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.

CVE-2026-48937 is a denial of service in the Node.js HTTP/2 server: when nghttp2 ended a session itself on a protocol error and sent a GOAWAY frame, Node.js was not told, so the session was never cleaned up and kept accepting data after the GOAWAY. Node.js fixed it for 24.x in 24.17.0, released 2026-06-18: the June 2026 security release, https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/june-2026-security-releases, lists 24.x among the affected release lines, and the 24.17.0 release notes, https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v24.17.0, list this CVE. The fix is commit https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/a8a0d12875 ('deps: fix integration issues with the latest nghttp2'), which carries CVE-ID: CVE-2026-48937 and is in the v24.17.0 tag and not in v24.16.0; outside tests it changes src/node_http2.cc and src/node_http2.h so that a GOAWAY nghttp2 sends on its own raises a protocol error and tears the session down. It ships with the bundled nghttp2 update to 1.69.0 in the same release (commit https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/66e6203c1c). The CVE record, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-48937, lists Node.js 24 releases up to 24.16.0 as affected. The DHI nodejs-24 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from the upstream Node.js release tarball for their version. They use the nghttp2 library bundled in that tarball: the node binary has no libnghttp2 dependency (it needs only libstdc++, libgcc_s and the musl C library). Each published nodejs-24 package holds one file, /usr/bin/node, a dynamically linked musl program that carries the Node.js JavaScript library and the C++ runtime where this code lives; the nodejs-24-dev subpackages hold C and C++ header files and two .gypi build configuration files under /usr/include/node, and the nodejs-24-doc subpackages hold the node man page and two debugger helper files, gdbinit and lldb_commands.py, with no ELF, PE or Mach-O file in either. We checked the node binary, /usr/bin/node, in every nodejs-24 package for Alpine 3.23 published by 2026-11-28, on x86_64 and aarch64 (checksums verified against the package index): 24.17.0-r0, 24.18.0-r0, 24.18.1-r0, 24.19.0-r0, 24.20.0-r0, 24.21.0-r0, 24.22.0-r0, 24.22.1-r0, 24.22.1-r1, 24.22.2-r0 and 24.22.3-r0 report v24.17.0 through v24.22.3 and carry the fix, while the earlier builds 24.13.0-r0, 24.13.1-r0, 24.14.0-r0, 24.14.1-r0, 24.15.0-r0, 24.15.0-r1 and 24.16.0-r0 report v24.13.0 through v24.16.0 and are affected. As a check, the node binary contains the 'nghttp2 session terminated internally' debug message this fix adds in 24.17.0-r0 and every later build on both architectures, and does not in any earlier build; the nghttp2 version string it embeds is 1.69.0 (24.17.0-r0 to 24.19.0-r0) or 1.70.0 (24.20.0-r0 and later), against 1.67.1 (24.13.0-r0) and 1.68.0 (24.13.1-r0 to 24.16.0-r0) in the affected builds. 24.17.0-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.
